hook: SCP-1844 is a pit in the Levant that has to be prayed over without pause, and much of the file is a roster of clergy from many traditions plus a long historical log of those who kept watch. Skim the table if you like, but don't skip the two short memos at the very end. Some log entries describe monstrous things climbing out and attacking staff, and the roster lists snake-handling and animal sacrifice among the containment duties.
whyItMatters: It is a strong example of the Foundation treating faith as engineering: piety is screened and measured in units, prayers are assigned like shifts, and every improvement is logged as a percentage. The long timeline sets the containment inside recorded history, with pharaohs, Roman generals, caliphs, popes and Napoleon all choosing to leave the rite alone or reinforce it. That cooperation between rival faiths is a large part of the appeal.
thingsToNotice: Read the log as a slow story of tightening control: heat-shielded gear brings the rite into the pit, closed capsules spare the crews from seeing what is inside, noise reduction lowers suicides, and breaches like the many-horned lamb of 1923 and the gaunt rider on a white horse in 1939 fade out until the object is downgraded to Euclid. Footnotes add that the capsules use an amplifier engineered from SCP-2167 and that three crew lost in 1955 were only recovered through SCP-2336. The closing exchange turns all that progress into dread. The director boasts that nobody is being burned or taken anymore, while his Jesuit assistant warns that contrathaumaturgic pressure is building under the pit at 99.6% efficacy and that a burst boiler is far worse than a leak, and the article stops there.

related.note: A footnote says the capsules' audio amplifier was engineered by studying it.
A footnote says three crew lost in the 1955 breach were eventually returned through it.
